relations.mechanism: AMPK also hits mTORC1 directly by phosphorylating Raptor, imposing a metabolic checkpoint independent of TSC.
relations.mechanism_beginner: AMPK also hits mTORC1 directly, adding a second, energy-based checkpoint on top of TSC.
relations.context: The Raptor arm is the TSC2-independent route, which is why it is measurable in TSC-null cells. Its relative contribution versus the TSC2 arm varies by cell type and by how deep the energy stress is.

relations.mechanism: Everolimus is rapamycin with a solubilising side chain - same FKBP12 mechanism, better oral pharmacokinetics. It is the molecule that carried this pathway into routine clinical use.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Everolimus is rapamycin with a small chemical tweak that makes it easier to take as a pill – same mechanism, better drug.
relations.note: Six trials behind one arrow. They establish the clinical effect of the drug; the allosteric mechanism itself rests on the rapamycin biochemistry.

relations.mechanism: Only when it is carrying rapamycin, FKBP12 docks on the FRB domain next to mTOR's active site. The FKBP12-rapamycin complex, not FKBP12 alone, is what blocks access for some substrates but not all; FKBP12 without the drug does not inhibit mTORC1. The inhibitory arrow is drawn from rapamycin (RAPA-MTORC1).
relations.mechanism_beginner: Only when it carries rapamycin does FKBP12 dock on mTORC1; the pair then blocks some, but not all, of what mTORC1 does. FKBP12 on its own does nothing to mTORC1.

relations.mechanism: In the canonical nutrient-dependent route, mTORC1 has to reach the lysosomal surface to be switched on, because that is where Rheb is waiting. Force it elsewhere and amino acids stop mattering. The requirement is stated for this route, not for every pool of mTOR in the cell.
relations.mechanism_beginner: In the amino-acid route, mTORC1 only works while it's sitting on the lysosome, because that is where its activator waits – move it somewhere else and amino acids stop being able to reach it.
relations.boundary: Scoped to amino-acid-driven activation. Live BRET imaging in this corpus (BOU2020) resolves mTOR activity in the cytosol, at the lysosome, in the nucleus and near mitochondria, so mTOR signalling is measurably not one pool. This map draws the lysosomal route and keeps the other localisations declared as open rather than asserting there are none. FER2024 refines this further: lysosomal mTORC1 (fed by local lysosomal proteolysis) and cytoplasmic mTORC1 (fed by exogenous amino acids) phosphorylate distinct downstream substrates — the lysosome is required for one regulatory sub-pool of mTORC1, not for all of it.

relations.mechanism: Metformin also inhibits mTORC1 WITHOUT going through AMPK: the effect survives in AMPK-null and TSC1/2-null cells and instead requires the Rag GTPases. This is the arm usually left out of the 'metformin works via AMPK' summary.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Metformin can also block mTORC1 through a completely separate route that doesn't need AMPK at all – a route often left out of the simple "metformin works via AMPK" story.
relations.context: Dose is the whole argument. Concentrations used in cell culture are typically far above plasma levels achieved at clinical doses, so in vitro mechanism may not describe what metformin does in a patient.
relations.boundary: Runs in parallel with METFORMIN-AMPK, not instead of it. The relative weight of the two routes in humans is unresolved.
relations.note: FOR2010 was removed from this edge on 2026-09-21: it measured hepatic gluconeogenesis and never read out mTORC1. It remains correctly cited in the boundary of METFORMIN-AMPK.

relations.mechanism: mTORC1 phosphorylates 4E-BP1, which lets go of eIF4E and frees cap-dependent translation. Rapamycin blocks this arm only partially - the origin of the whole 'rapamycin-resistant output' problem.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC1 tags 4E-BP1 so it lets go of another protein, freeing up protein-building – but the standard drug (rapamycin) only partly blocks this step.

relations.mechanism: mTORC1 phosphorylates and stabilises Grb10 - the start of a feedback loop that talks back to the insulin receptor.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC1 stabilises Grb10, kicking off a feedback loop that talks back to the insulin receptor.

relations.mechanism: Lowering mTORC1 activity extends lifespan across yeast, worms, flies and mice - one of the most conserved interventions in ageing biology, alongside dietary restriction.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Turning mTORC1 down extends lifespan in yeast, worms, flies and mice – one of the most universal anti-ageing effects known.
relations.context: Strongly modified by sex, strain, diet and the age at which inhibition starts. Effect direction is reproducible; effect size is not transferable between models.
relations.boundary: No human hard-endpoint evidence. This is the Atlas's flagged 'human endpoint desert'.

relations.mechanism: A second feedback arm: inhibiting mTORC1 releases a PI3K-dependent brake and MAPK signalling goes up. Together with S6K1-IRS1 this is why single-agent mTOR inhibition tends to be met by compensatory growth signalling.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Blocking mTORC1 can backfire by releasing a brake on a different growth pathway (MAPK) – one reason mTOR-blocking drugs alone often aren't enough.
relations.boundary: Single-study edge in this corpus.
relations.note: CAR2008 was already in the corpus but carried no edge until 2026-07-29.

relations.mechanism: mTORC1 raises mitochondrial output two ways: through a YY1-PGC-1alpha transcription complex, and by relieving 4E-BP so mitochondrial proteins get translated.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC1 boosts the cell's mitochondria – its power plants – two ways at once: through a gene-activating complex, and by freeing up 4E-BP.
relations.boundary: Shown in cultured cells and skeletal muscle (CUN2007) and mammalian cell lines (MOR2013). One organismal result points the other way: adipose-specific Raptor deletion raised mitochondrial respiration (POL2008), see MTORC1-OXPHOS.

relations.mechanism: mTORC1 couples nucleotide supply to demand - it turns on purine synthesis through the mitochondrial tetrahydrofolate cycle so a dividing cell can actually copy its DNA.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC1 turns on the machinery for building DNA/RNA building blocks, so a growing cell can actually copy its DNA.

relations.mechanism: Blocking mTOR reversed Akt-driven pre-cancerous prostate lesions in mice, showing the growth was mTORC1-dependent and reversible.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Blocking mTOR reversed early, pre-cancerous prostate changes in mice caused by an overactive growth signal.
relations.boundary: Scope: the lesion was prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia, a pre-cancerous stage, driven by transgenic human AKT1 in mice, and the drug (RAD001) inhibits mTORC1 allosterically. Mouse only in this corpus. Not a demonstration in established prostate cancer.
relations.note: The arrow means mTORC1 inhibition reversed a pre-cancerous prostate lesion in a mouse model. It is not a claim that mTORC1 drives established prostate cancer.

relations.mechanism: Renal cancers frequently carry lesions that leave mTORC1 constitutively active - which is why this tissue responds to mTOR inhibitors at all, and why an exceptional responder could be traced to TSC1 loss.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Many kidney cancers carry mutations that leave mTORC1 stuck "on" – that's why this cancer type responds to mTOR-blocking drugs at all, though it doesn't prove mTORC1 causes the cancer.
relations.boundary: Correlative plus one n-of-1 genomic case (IYE2012); not a demonstration that mTORC1 activation initiates RCC.
relations.note: Replaces TUMOR-RCC, which asserted 'Tumor growth activates RCC' - a category error, since RCC is an instance of tumour growth, not a downstream target.

relations.mechanism: mTORC1 phosphorylates S6K1, switching on the translation machinery. This is the classic rapamycin-sensitive output and the readout most papers actually measure.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC1 switches on S6K1, which turns on the cell's protein-building machinery – the classic effect most studies of this drug class measure.
relations.context: Standard mTORC1 readout, but a readout is not the whole output. S6K1 phosphorylation is fully rapamycin-sensitive while 4E-BP1 is not, so 'mTORC1 activity' measured by S6K1 alone systematically overstates how much rapamycin inhibits mTORC1.
relations.boundary: Caution: p-S6K is a proxy, not the phenotype. Many 'mTORC1 activity' claims rest on this single band.
relations.note: Worth flagging on the page: readout != outcome.

relations.mechanism: mTORC1 sustains the inflammatory secretory output of cells that are already senescent, by promoting IL1A translation. Inhibiting it quietens that output without reversing the proliferative arrest.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC1 keeps old, "senescent" cells pumping out inflammatory signals, and blocking it calms that output down without making those cells young again. Whether mTORC1 also helps push cells into senescence in the first place is a separate question this arrow does not answer.
relations.boundary: Three studies, all in cells or a rat disease model. LAB2015 and NAR2011 measure the secretory output of cells that are already senescent (IL1A translation; IL-6/IL-8 production fuelled by mTOR at the TASCC). CHEN2026C (human disc cells, rat needle-puncture model) shows mTORC1 hyperactivation after TSC2 loss together with senescence and SASP, both blocked by rapamycin - a disease-model result, not a general demonstration that mTORC1 drives cells into senescence. That is why this arrow lands on the secretory programme and not on senescence itself.
relations.note: The arrow means mTORC1 sustains the secretory output (SASP) of senescent cells. Whether mTORC1 also pushes cells into senescence in the first place (geroconversion) is a separate and weaker claim that this edge does not make.

relations.mechanism: mTORC1 drives the SREBP transcription factors, which turn on the genes for making fat and cholesterol - growth needs membrane, not just protein.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC1 switches on SREBP, the genes that build fat and cholesterol – a growing cell needs membrane material, not just protein.

relations.mechanism: Active mTORC1 phosphorylates TFEB right on the lysosomal surface, trapping it in the cytoplasm. Switch mTORC1 off and TFEB walks into the nucleus.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Active mTORC1 tags TFEB and traps it outside the nucleus; switch mTORC1 off and TFEB moves in.
relations.context: Substrate-selective. Depends on FLCN/FNIP RagC/D status, so mTORC1 can be active on S6K1 while not phosphorylating TFEB.
relations.boundary: RagD specifically (more than RagC) promotes TFEB/TFE3 phosphorylation via tighter LAMTOR binding — GOL2022 shows this is paralogue-specific, not a generic Rag-dimer property.
relations.note: Four independent studies - one of the best-supported output edges.

relations.mechanism: Hyperactive mTORC1 reprograms translation toward a specific set of pro-growth and pro-metastasis mRNAs (HSI2012, prostate models) and couples nucleotide synthesis to demand, creating a targetable vulnerability in TSC-deficient cells (VAL2017).
relations.mechanism_beginner: Hyperactive mTORC1 pushes cells to build a specific set of growth- and spread-promoting proteins – the tumour becomes hooked on that programme.
relations.boundary: Context-dependent: shown in genetically driven mouse tumour models and cancer cell lines with hyperactive mTORC1 (PTEN loss, TSC loss), not as a general property of tumours.
relations.note: The arrow means hyperactive mTORC1 promotes tumour growth where the pathway is already unleashed - PTEN-loss and TSC-loss backgrounds. It is not a claim that mTORC1 activity causes tumours generally, and normal mTORC1 signalling is not a tumour driver here.

relations.mechanism: Active mTORC1 phosphorylates ULK1 at an inhibitory site, holding autophagy shut while nutrients are plentiful.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Active mTORC1 tags ULK1 to hold it back, keeping the cell's self-cleanup process (autophagy) switched off while nutrients are plentiful.

relations.mechanism: Unphosphorylated PRAS40 sits in the substrate groove of mTORC1 and blocks it - a built-in plug.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Untagged PRAS40 sits inside mTORC1 and blocks it, like a built-in plug.

relations.mechanism: The active Rag dimer grabs Raptor and physically drags mTORC1 to the lysosomal surface. This is a relocation, not an activation - the kinase is moved to where its activator waits.
relations.mechanism_beginner: The switched-on Rag proteins grab mTORC1 and drag it to the lysosome. This moves it into place; it doesn't turn it on by itself.
relations.boundary: Rag paralogues are not interchangeable: RagC/D sets substrate specificity downstream (RagD favors TFEB/TFE3 phosphorylation via tighter LAMTOR binding, while both Rags are involved for non-lysosomal substrates like S6K), and RagA/B sets the response to amino acid withdrawal (RagB-expressing cells keep mTORC1 lysosomal and active even when starved) — GOL2022.
relations.note: The conceptual crux of the whole route: teach recruitment vs activation as two separate ideas.

relations.mechanism: Raptor is the subunit that defines mTORC1 and presents substrates to the kinase.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Raptor is the piece that makes mTORC1 what it is, and hands it the targets it needs to act on.

relations.mechanism: GTP-loaded Rheb binds mTORC1 at the lysosome and physically re-shapes its active site into the working conformation.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Switched-on Rheb docks onto mTORC1 and physically reshapes it into its working form – the actual "on" switch.
relations.context: Rheb must be GTP-loaded and co-located with mTORC1. Rheb is also distributed across the ER and Golgi, and which pool supplies the activating Rheb is unresolved.
relations.note: Convergence point: the amino-acid route delivers mTORC1 here, the growth-factor route delivers Rheb. Both required.

relations.mechanism: Salr suppresses mTORC1-driven growth downstream of stress signalling.
relations.mechanism_beginner: This stress-induced protein suppresses mTORC1-driven growth once stress signalling turns it on.

relations.mechanism: Temsirolimus is the intravenous rapamycin analogue, and, to our knowledge, the first mTOR inhibitor to show an overall-survival benefit in a randomised trial.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Temsirolimus is the IV version of rapamycin, and the first mTOR-blocking drug shown to help patients live longer in a controlled trial.

relations.mechanism: The TSC complex is the pathway's main tumour suppressor. Inherit one broken copy and lesions grow wherever the second copy is lost - the clearest human evidence that mTORC1 activity drives tissue overgrowth.
relations.mechanism_beginner: The TSC brake is the pathway's main tumour-suppressor. Inherit one broken copy of the gene and growths appear wherever the second copy is also lost. (This arrow skips a step for simplicity – TSC actually acts through Rheb first.)
relations.context: Deliberately compressed: TSC acts on Rheb rather than directly on mTORC1. Kept as one link so the overview reads cleanly.
relations.note: This is the edge that turns the biochemistry into a disease.

relations.mechanism: Rapamycin inhibits mTORC1 only as a complex with FKBP12: the pair docks on the FRB domain beside the active site and blocks some substrates but not all, so S6K1 phosphorylation collapses while much of 4E-BP1 phosphorylation persists.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Rapamycin, carried by its helper protein FKBP12, jams part of mTORC1 – it blocks some of what mTORC1 does but not all of it.
relations.boundary: Directness is graded indirect because the mechanism requires FKBP12, as for everolimus and the bi-sterics. Acute effect only; the chronic effect on mTORC2 is the separate RAPA-MTORC2 edge.

relations.mechanism: A second and contested way in: JEW2015 reports that glutamine activates mTORC1 without the Rag GTPases, through Arf1, and that leucine and glutamine therefore do not share one entry point. If it holds, Rag-dependent lysosomal recruitment is not the only route to the kinase.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Some experiments say glutamine has a second way in that skips the Rag proteins entirely. If that is right, the lysosome story is not the whole story – which is a big claim resting on thin evidence.
relations.boundary: Cell-type dependent and not uniformly reproduced across labs. The Rag-dependent route is the separate GLN-RAG edge; neither edge should be read as covering the other.

relations.claim: Resistance exercise / mechanical load activates mTORC1
relations.mechanism: Mechanical loading raises mTORC1 signalling in skeletal muscle. Rapamycin given to human volunteers blocks the contraction-induced increase in muscle protein synthesis, placing mTORC1 causally between the load and the response.
relations.boundary: Compressed: load reaches mTORC1 through several routes, only some of which need IGF-1, and the map draws one arrow. The human evidence establishes that mTORC1 is required, not which upstream route carries the signal.

relations.mechanism: Reduced nutrient and energy availability lowers mTORC1 signalling through the amino-acid and energy arms simultaneously – the sensors detect scarcity, and AMPK detects the falling energy charge.
relations.boundary: Supporting evidence here is thinner than the claim's reputation. ROM2016 (two-year caloric restriction is tolerable in non-obese humans) and MAT2017 (rhesus survival) were removed as support in the 2026-09-21 audit because neither measured mTORC1; they belong to the CR-LONGEVITY edge, not to this one. SOL2014 found macronutrient RATIO mattered more than total intake in mice, so 'caloric restriction' may be the wrong variable name.

relations.mechanism: Occupies the mTOR active site in competition with ATP, so inhibition does not depend on obstructing substrate access and is not partial in the way rapalog inhibition is.
relations.boundary: Cell-line pharmacology. Clinical development of this class has been limited by toxicity attributed to simultaneous mTORC2 inhibition, which is precisely what the bi-steric design tries to avoid.

relations.mechanism: A bivalent molecule engages an FKBP12-dependent site and the active site simultaneously, producing deeper mTORC1 inhibition than a rapalog while sparing mTORC2.
relations.boundary: Phase 1 in advanced solid tumours – a safety and pharmacodynamic result, not an efficacy verdict. Directness is graded indirect because, like rapalogs, the mechanism requires FKBP12. Consensus is emerging: one trial, newest evidence in the corpus.

relations.mechanism: Genome-wide CRISPR screens identify at least two parallel relays carrying mitochondrial dysfunction to mTORC1: AMPK, and the heme-regulated inhibitor HRI acting through the integrated stress response.
relations.mechanism_beginner: When mitochondria – the cell's power plants – are damaged, at least two separate alarm signals reach mTORC1 to shut it down.
relations.boundary: CRISPR screening in cell lines; the relative weight of the AMPK and HRI arms in tissue is untested.

relations.mechanism: mTORC1 raises mitochondrial respiratory capacity through a YY1–PGC-1α transcriptional programme and through 4E-BP-dependent translation of respiratory components.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC1 boosts how much energy mitochondria can produce, through both gene activation and protein-building. One mouse experiment points the other way – removing mTORC1 from fat tissue RAISED respiration – so this direction is not settled in a living animal.
relations.boundary: Effect size varies strongly by tissue; the transcriptional and translational arms have not been cleanly separated in vivo. OVERLAP (audit 2026-09-04): this edge and MTORC1-MITO assert overlapping biology from overlapping citations (CUN2007, MOR2013) at different tiers and different consensus levels. Read them together; they are not independent support.

relations.mechanism: mTOR interacts with YY1 and is required for the YY1–PGC-1α complex to drive mitochondrial gene expression; rapamycin lowers both the transcripts and oxygen consumption.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTOR works together with a gene-activating team to switch on mitochondrial genes – a rare example of this pathway acting inside the nucleus rather than at the cell's outer edges. The direct interaction rests on a single study in this Atlas.
relations.boundary: Single-study support in this corpus for the direct interaction; the downstream respiratory phenotype is better replicated than the binding itself.

relations.mechanism: Unleashing mTORC1 by deleting TSC1 drives quiescent haematopoietic stem cells into cycle, raises mitochondrial biogenesis and floods them with ROS; an antioxidant rescues self-renewal.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Switching mTORC1 on too much pushes resting stem cells to start dividing and floods them with reactive, damaging molecules; giving them antioxidants restores their normal function.
relations.boundary: Demonstrated in haematopoietic stem cells, where quiescence is the baseline state. Cell types that are already cycling need not behave this way.

relations.mechanism: Oxidative stress activates a redox-sensitive PI3K–Akt–mTORC1–eIF4A cascade that selectively promotes cap-dependent translation of P-glycoprotein.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Oxidative damage can itself switch on mTORC1 through a chain of signals, closing a feedback loop that can turn a brief stress into a lasting one.
relations.boundary: One cell-line study in a multidrug-resistance context; whether the loop runs in normal physiology at these ROS levels is untested.

relations.mechanism: mTOR inhibition reverses Akt-driven prostate intraepithelial neoplasia partly through HIF-1-dependent pathways, placing HIF-1α downstream of mTORC1 in this setting.
relations.mechanism_beginner: In one specific setting (prostate cells), mTORC1 turns on a factor usually associated with low oxygen – here it's mTORC1 driving it, not the other way around.
relations.boundary: Mouse prostate model with pharmacological mTOR inhibition; HIF-1α is one of several pathways implicated in the same experiment.

relations.mechanism: Active mTORC1, acting through the transcription factor c-MYC, raises production of MAT2A, the enzyme that makes SAM, so a growing cell makes more of its main methyl donor.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC1 tells the cell to make more SAM.
relations.boundary: Human cell lines and mouse xenograft tumours; acts through c-MYC on MAT2A. Together with SAM-SAMTOR this forms a loop whose behaviour in normal tissue is untested. Single study.
